title: engineering-all-hands-2026-05-06
content:
Engineering All-Hands - 2026-05-06
Owner: Aisha Patel
Attendees: eng org + SRE reps (see collaborators)
Status: in_review

Agenda:
- Quick metrics + health check
- Major releases / rollouts this week
- Incident summary (May 3 partial outage) + RCA status
- Team highlights (Serving Runtime, Platform, Console, Private Deployments, SRE)
- Hiring / ramp update
- Action items / next steps

Quick metrics (rolling 7d where noted):
- Host API overall success rate: 99.93% (target >= 99.9%)
- P95 latency (text generation, prod): 210ms (improved from 238ms week-over-week after batching kernel changes)
- Avg tokens/sec per GPU: +8% vs last week under v1.18 canary
- Dedicated utilization: 72% average, peak 89% (EU region saw higher peaks due to batch job spikes)
- Cost per 1k tokens (hosted): down ~6% after batching+kv-cache tuning

Notes: numbers are preliminary; Finance will publish finalized cost metrics on Friday.

Major releases / rollouts
- Serving Runtime v1.18 rolled to canary and 60% of prod on 2026-05-04. Key changes: continuous batching improvements, kernel selector heuristics, KV-cache eviction policy tweaks. Early telemetry: p95 latency down ~12% for short-context requests.
- Console: rollout 2026-05-05 (feature flags) for better per-route cost breakdown and trace linking (PR #211). UX feedback: minor alignment issues on the cost table - Ellen will file the follow-up.
- Dedicated autoscaler patch (hotfix) deployed to staging; addressing flapping seen in EU reserved pools. Patch linked: ENG-4198. Schedule: staging validation this week, prod rollout Monday 2026-05-11 if green.

Incident summary (May 3 partial outage) - Tl;dr
- Impact: ~45 minutes of elevated 5xx errors for hosted API (region: us-west-2), ~0.4% of global requests affected. Some customer sessions saw degraded streaming behavior.
- Root cause (current hypothesis): bug in KV-cache eviction path under high memory pressure leading to repeated model reload attempts + transient worker crashes.
- Timeline:
  - 09:11 UTC: first elevated error alerts
  - 09:18 UTC: SRE triggers mitigation (throttle rollout + circuit breaker for cache eviction)
  - 09:56 UTC: traffic normalized after temporary throttles and extra worker spin-up
- Mitigations in place: conservative eviction thresholds, stronger circuit breaker around model reload, temporary increase of worker pool in affected region.
- RCA status: draft RCA is in progress (ENG-4123). Next update expected 2026-05-08.
- Action: add an automated canary test that simulates memory pressure across the KV-cache path (owner: Marcus).

Team highlights / dept updates
- Serving Runtime (Diego): v1.18 shows good perf gains. Follow-ups: investigate a KV-cache regression where under specific sequence-length distributions the cache miss rate increased (small cohort). Diego to lead root-cause and backport fix if needed.
- Platform Engineering (this team): working on routing policies for cost-aware fallbacks. Prototype ready; internal demo next week. Also prepping infra for the Dedicated autoscaler patch.
- Console & Rollouts (Ellen): new cost breakdown landed; UX polish scheduled. Adding a per-model token distribution heatmap (designs ready).
- Private Deployments (Nina): onboarding for ACME Financial is in legal review; technical dry-run in staging scheduled 2026-05-12. Private package now supports HSM key-wrap integration (early tests passed).
- SRE (Tomás): post-incident improvements: better alert grouping, new playbook entry for KV-cache incidents, and a quicker rollback pathway for runtime upgrades. Also running chaos test for autoscaler behavior 2026-05-09.

Hiring / org
- Remaining open IC roles: 3 backend infra, 2 runtime engineers, 1 product manager. Recruiting making good progress - 2 offers extended (serving-runtime and observability).
- Reminder: keep interview loop feedback consolidated in Greenhouse; hiring bar doc updated last week.

Unresolved questions / decisions needed
- Should we make the conservative KV-cache eviction thresholds permanent or gate behind a config toggle? Pros/cons discussed; decision needed by 2026-05-10 (owner: Diego + SRE).
- Autoscaler patch rollout window: Monday 5/11 vs Wed 5/13. Ops prefers Monday to avoid business-peak spike; PMs prefer Wednesday to allow more validation. Vote in #platform-ops by EOD 2026-05-07.

Action items (owner - due)
- Marcus Nguyen: implement automated memory-pressure canary for KV-cache path (ENG-4123) - due 2026-05-08
- Diego Ramirez: deep-dive KV-cache miss-regression and prepare hotfix/backport plan - due 2026-05-09
- Ellen Cho: file UX follow-up for cost table alignment and schedule quick UX pass - due 2026-05-08
- Nina Sinha: complete staging dry-run for ACME private deployment + checklist to legal - due 2026-05-12
- Tomás Rivera: run chaos autoscaler test and post results in #sre-runbooks - due 2026-05-09
- Aisha Patel: publish finalized cost metrics with finance and send all-hands summary to product + execs - due 2026-05-08

Notes to self / working items (informal)
- Need to coordinate with sales on messaging for ACME on security posture (KMS/HSM notes).
- Flag for follow-up: check if EU batch job spikes correlate with nightly retraining tasks (might need tenant throttling).

Next all-hands: 2026-05-13 16:00 UTC (tentative)

References / links:
- Incident ticket & draft RCA: ENG-4123
- Autoscaler patch: ENG-4198
- Serving Runtime PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/349
- Console PR (cost table): https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/211

End of notes.
